name: Original creatures
description: Original small expressive characters, the 'Pips': a smooth sculpted bean body, a dark glass visor whose glowing face acts (squints, widens, droops, lip-syncs), an antenna bulb that reacts to mood, mitten hands, boots, optional headset. A cosy maker workshop with a pegboard, bench, shelves and warm hanging bulbs. Explainers about tools, AI helpers and how things work.
rules: The visor face is the acting: eyes squint, widen, droop and look at things; the mouth follows the voice; the antenna bulb brightens on emphasis.
Each Pip has ONE body colour, the same cream belly and mitten hands, dark boots; a team is told apart by colour, antenna, headset and badge.
Smooth clay surfaces with a soft sheen: no hard edges on the characters, rounded props in the world.
Warm practical light (hanging bulbs, bench lamp) against a cool teal wall; the character always has a cool rim light.
Orange and cream characters stand on teal: keep that complementary pairing.
Small body, big head: arms are short, so objects sit at 0.55 m and the actor reaches with the near hand.
Captions: bold white, thick dark outline, one amber word.
camera_language: Small characters want a low, close camera at their eye level so they feel big and alive. Wide only to place them in the workshop; medium for talking (the visor face is the performance); medium-wide three-quarter to show what the hands are doing. Moves only on a reveal or a realisation, each with a reason.
audio_direction: upbeat bed, boing on hops, pop on text
pitfalls: Over-the-shoulder shows only the round back: use medium-wide three-quarter.
At close-up the face crops: use medium-close-up for reactions.
The bright bulb on the antenna can bloom into the frame top: keep the camera lower than 1.1 m or bloom threshold above 0.85.
references: reference videos ref1, ref4, ref7 (creature idea only)
